description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports many short streaming responses that terminate 200-800ms after reconnect when the client rebinds keepalive/session on the same TCP socket. The responses are valid JSON fragments but missing the terminal 'done' event; client observes partial outputs and no final choice.

Impact:
- Intermittent for a subset (~2-3%) of requests from Nimbus Retail dedicated pool in us-west-2.
- Affects production chat experience; customer reports higher user retries and UX regressions.
- No billing discrepancy reported, but operational cost increased due to retries.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity, prod/us-west-2, edge via ALB -> edge-proxy -> streaming-proxy -> serving-runtime.
- Clients use SSE fallback (long-lived HTTP keepalives) and sometimes reuse sockets during network handoffs.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Open SSE stream from client behind corporate NAT with aggressive keepalive probes.
2) Trigger network change (phone network -> wifi) or NAT port refresh, resulting in socket reuse + server-side keepalive rebind.
3) Client resumes session; server sends resumed chunks but stream closes early (~200-800ms) without terminal event.

Observed behavior:
- Stream body contains truncated token sequences and final JSON delimiter never arrives.
- Edge logs show a 200 response and connection close at the reverse proxy with no 5xx.
- Streaming-proxy logs include a resume handshake, but the resume offset in the resume message is lower than the worker's expected sequence due to clock/sequence skew.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should stitch and deliver full final chunk including terminal event.

Relevant logs / snippets:
- edge-proxy: 2026-03-12T17:22:41Z ALB-conn reset after keepalive probe (conn_id=ab12c)
- streaming-proxy: 2026-03-12T17:22:41Z resume-request from client session_id=ns-94 uid=987
- streaming-proxy: 2026-03-12T17:22:41Z resume-offset=1583412345 (client-ts) expected-offset=1583412347 worker-window-start=1583412347
- serving-runtime: 2026-03-12T17:22:41Z delivered-chunk seq=1583412346 size=1234 partial=true

Attachments:
- Customer provided HAR-equivalent trace, socket lifecycle timeline, and sample truncated payload (attached to ticket).
comments: 2026-03-12 17:35 - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged and escalated to streaming team. Requested packet capture and sample truncated payload from Nimbus. SLA flagged as P1.

2026-03-12 18:02 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Observed matching resume-offset/expected-offset mismatch in edge logs. Suspect offset space derived from epoch-timestamp glue in proxy code path. Routing to runtime/streaming-proxy owners.

2026-03-12 20:14 - Nimbus Dev (customer): We reproduced this with a scripted NAT refresh. Attached tokenized payloads; behavior consistent across redwood-1-small and starling-v2 endpoints. Happy to share pcap on request.

2026-03-13 09:30 - Priya Kapoor (Streaming Eng): Reproduced locally with test harness that simulates keepalive rebind. Observed sequence id wrap/skew when proxy translates session offsets to worker sequence using an incorrect base (client timestamp vs server counter). Opening PR to add stricter validation of resume offsets.

2026-03-14 11:05 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Temporary mitigation: enable conservative resume timeout for Nimbus dedicated pool and force full-session re-fetch on detected offset mismatch. Not ideal but reduces customer-visible truncations by ~85% in canary.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: resume offset is interpreted as an absolute timestamp by streaming-proxy; during socket rebind client sends offset derived from client-side epoch which can differ by small amounts leading to worker rejecting trailing tokens as out-of-window.
Hypothesis 2: edge-proxy's keepalive rebind preserves TCP 4-tuple and the streaming-proxy treats it as same session, but internal session ID mapping collides causing stale KV-state to be applied.

Reproduction: test harness that simulates NAT port change + keepalive rebind reproduces truncated stream consistently when resume message carries offset derived from client-time instead of resume-seq. Local repro attached to PR.
Metrics: canary on 3 nodes in us-west-2 showed truncation rate drop from 2.6% -> 0.4% after conservative timeout mitigation; still investigating root fix.
Correlated issues: similar offset-check logic referenced in SUP-314159 runbook; difference is this customer uses a dedicated pool which surfaces race more frequently.
resolution: Workaround applied: enabled conservative resume timeout and forced full reissue on offset mismatch for Nimbus dedicated pool (rolled to 5% of capacity on 2026-03-13, then 30% on 2026-03-14).

Planned fix: streaming-proxy PR to change resume-offset validation to use server-sequence base (https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-proxy/pull/5423). Target for rollout to prod-canary: 2026-03-21.
Postmortem action items: (1) add unit/integration tests for keepalive-rebind path, (2) add telemetry for resume-offset skew occurrences, (3) update runbook with immediate rollback steps.
